clue.text: Alloy with fictitious disease featured in scientific study

parts.note: an alloy such as brass or bronze is a metal
the lurgy is a jokey British name for an imaginary illness, 'the dreaded lurgy'

explanation.surface: A paper on alloys has been padded out with a made-up illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The dreaded lurgy' is everyday British slang for a vague, invented bug that is going round.
explanation.definitionFit: Metallurgy is the branch of science dealing with the properties and working of metals.

clue.text: Married outside the circle — and ditched!

indicators.note: outside says the word for married wraps around the letter for the circle

parts.note: mated means married or paired
a circle is drawn like the letter O

explanation.surface: A married couple stand outside the circle and are dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditched' reads as 'abandoned', but here it means having a ditch, as a castle surrounded by water does.
explanation.definitionFit: A moated building is surrounded by a defensive trench, so it is literally ditched.

clue.text: Repetitious expression of irritation

indicators.note: repetitious tells us the short exclamation is said twice over

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of mild annoyance

explanation.surface: Someone keeps clicking their tongue in annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubled tut is the standard written form of a disapproving tongue-click.

clue.text: Cold compartment in pantry?

parts.note: a chilled storage unit kept in the food store room, named by the room and the appliance together

explanation.surface: Someone asks where the cool storage space in a kitchen cupboard is.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerator without a freezer section, designed to keep food cool like a traditional cold store.

clue.text: Bear up?

parts.note: read as a bear found up in the night sky, the Latin name of the constellations Great and Little Bear

explanation.surface: An encouragement to stay strong through hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear up' looks like 'keep your spirits up', but it means a bear that is up above, among the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa is Latin for a she-bear and names the northern constellations Major and Minor.

clue.text: Where to sit out coming from great sedan

indicators.note: coming from says the letters are drawn out of the following words and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A place to rest outdoors salvaged from a fine old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A bench placed in the yard or lawn is where you sit outdoors.

clue.text: Resort has mass of junk-mail

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
m is the scientific abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A holiday resort sends out piles of unwanted mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is the common term for unsolicited bulk email.

clue.text: Leave cockney lady behind, she's a witness

parts.note: to pass is to leave something alone or decline it
her with the h dropped, as a Cockney Londoner says it
by means past or behind, as in left by the wayside

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a London woman, who has seen it all happen.
explanation.walkthrough: Together the pieces say 'pass 'er by', literally leave her behind; Cockneys drop the h of her.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander who happens upon an incident can be called on as a witness to it.

clue.text: Think of remarkable meat diet

indicators.note: remarkable suggests something out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Consider an unusual all-meat eating plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to reflect deeply or ponder.

clue.text: To some extent following one type

parts.note: after means following
a means one, as in a single item
a sort is a type or kind

explanation.surface: Coming next is a particular kind, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in a rough or partial way, more or less.

clue.text: Ushered her out exhausted

indicators.note: out says the word for the woman is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: She was shown out of the room, worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted supplies are spent or consumed completely.

clue.text: Winsome blond, embarrassed, to impress very strongly

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests discomposure, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An attractive fair-haired person, red-faced, makes a great impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that astonishes or overwhelms you is said to have this effect.

clue.text: French duke in ebbing river had been pulled out

indicators.note: in places the French title inside the turned-round river
ebbing means flowing back, so the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and also one between England and Wales
duc is French for duke

explanation.surface: A French nobleman in a river at low tide had been dragged out.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebbing, a tide flowing back, suits a river and signals reading it backwards as EED; the French title then sits inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to draw forth or bring out something latent.

clue.text: Campanologist's temporary accommodation?

parts.note: a bell-ringer's portable shelter, named as if it belonged to someone who rings bells

explanation.surface: Asks where a bell-ringer stays on a short trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A conical canvas shelter held up by a single central pole, shaped like a bell.

clue.text: It is bound to help foreign traveller

definitions.text: It is bound to help foreign traveller

parts.words: It is bound to help foreign traveller
parts.note: bound means stitched into covers, not obliged: a volume of useful expressions for tourists abroad

explanation.surface: Something is certain to assist a tourist overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' reads as 'certain to', but it means made into a bound volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A small volume listing useful expressions with translations for tourists.

clue.text: How boffin who sat restlessly scored?

definitions.text: How boffin who sat restlessly scored?

indicators.note: restlessly suggests fidgeting and moving about, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Asks how a fidgety scientist managed to make runs.
explanation.walkthrough: BOFFIN is British slang for a scientist; the phrase comes from cricket, where runs scored by the batsman himself count to his own credit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means on one's own initiative, from runs credited to a batter personally.

clue.text: Forcibly expressive about the map I see, so to speak

indicators.note: about here means scattered around, so these letters are rearranged
so to speak means the word is said aloud and replaced by a letter of the same sound

parts.note: see is pronounced like the letter C

explanation.surface: A forceful speaker spouts on about the chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges THEMAPI into EMPHATI; 'so to speak' turns 'see' into the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic statement is made with force and conviction.

clue.text: None left, OK

explanation.surface: Everything is gone, and that is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'None left' reads as nothing remaining; cryptically it means everything is on the other side, none on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: If none are on the left, all are on the right; the phrase also means satisfactory or fine.

clue.text: On the island, first person with Georgia brown having soup

parts.note: Mull is an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides
I is the first person pronoun
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
tawny is an orange-brown colour

explanation.surface: A Hebridean visitor with a brown Georgian companion has a bowl of something hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy curry-flavoured broth of Anglo-Indian origin.

clue.text: Make disclosure about meat

parts.note: re means about or concerning
veal is meat from a calf

explanation.surface: Someone tells the truth about where the meat came from.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to make something known or uncover it.

clue.text: Amused oneself, having performed in the band perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone had a good time, having been a band member.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fun or engage in recreation, and also to have made music on an instrument.

clue.text: In there go especially fast and let us see what happens

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Get in there and be quick about it, and we will find out what comes.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across tHERE GO ESpecially; 'fast' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said just before trying something risky, wondering about the outcome.

clue.text: Besides being a toff

parts.note: a swell and a toff are both old British words for a smartly dressed upper-class man

explanation.surface: Someone is not only present but also a posh gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for an upper-class person, and SWELL is an old word for the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in addition or too.

clue.text: Second child to move sideways

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A younger child shuffles sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that skids slides sideways out of control.

clue.text: American takeaway in Africa?

explanation.surface: A fast-food order picked up somewhere on the African continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Food bought to go is the American phrase for carry-out; Togo is also a West African country.

clue.text: Make haste appear animated

explanation.surface: Hurry up and try to look lively.
explanation.definitionFit: The command means hurry up, and literally it means seem full of energy.

clue.text: Attractive reduction at end of sale

parts.note: a cut is a reduction, as in a price cut

indicators.note: at end of picks out only the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A tempting price drop on the last day of the sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means pretty or appealing in an endearing way.

clue.text: Scampered off with empty broken desk first

indicators.note: first says the rearranged piece goes at the front of the answer
broken means smashed apart, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: addled can mean empty, from an addled egg that will never hatch

explanation.surface: Someone ran off after the empty desk was found broken.
explanation.walkthrough: An addled egg is rotten and will never hatch, hence 'empty'; 'broken' scrambles the desk into SKED, and 'first' puts that in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is to run away hurriedly, an informal word for bolting.
